verdict: Membership growth pushed revenue up 26%, but medical costs ate nearly all of it — operating profit fell to $75M, and only a one-off joint-venture gain kept GAAP profit positive.

kpis.label: Benefit ratio
kpis.note: of premiums paid out as care

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: Premiums from 18.0 million medical members — mostly Medicare Advantage (6.5 million individual members) — plus Medicare Part D and Medicaid plans.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Services revenue, mainly CenterWell — senior primary care, home health and pharmacy services sold beyond Humana's own plans.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends earned on the cash and bond portfolio held against future claims.

opex.name: Operating costs
opex.note: The cost of running the plans and care businesses — staff, technology and administration. At 11.2% of revenue, this ratio improved as membership scaled.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear-and-tear charges on buildings, systems and intangibles.

otherDetail: Other income of $358M — dominated by a non-cash gain from restructuring the CenterWell senior primary care joint ventures into a new BlackRock partnership — less $217M of interest expense. A further $15M of equity-method losses sits between pre-tax income and net income.
follow100Note: The $100 chart nets the $358M of other income (mostly the joint-venture gain) and $217M of interest expense inside the profit line rather than as a cost row: before that net $141M boost, operations alone kept just $0.18 of every $100. Humana reports two business segments — Insurance ($39.1B of revenue, a $303M operating loss) and CenterWell ($7.2B, $243M of operating income) — which overlap, so the revenue lines above are used as the chart's sources because they sum to total revenue. Net income attributable to Humana was $162M, after a $1M loss belonging to non-controlling interests.

takeaways.title: Care costs ate the growth
takeaways.text: Benefits expense rose 30% to $36.3B — faster than premiums — as new Medicare members ran higher benefit ratios and favorable prior-period reserve development shrank to $67M from $275M.

takeaways.title: Membership is booming
takeaways.text: Total medical membership rose 20% to 18.0 million, with total Medicare membership up to 11.2 million — the growth behind the 26% revenue jump.

takeaways.title: Guidance still went up
takeaways.text: Despite the adjusted loss, Humana raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to at least $9.50 (from $9.00) and pointed to near-record 2027 Star Ratings averaging 4.17 stars.

oneTimers: GAAP profit includes a large non-cash gain from restructuring the CenterWell primary care joint ventures with a BlackRock affiliate (inside the $358M of other income) — excluding items like it, Humana lost $0.70 per share on an adjusted basis vs GAAP EPS of +$1.33.
The Insurance segment swung to a $303M operating loss (from a $251M profit), while CenterWell earned $243M.
